entities.name: Alonso de Covarrubias
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Alonso de Covarrubias (1488–1570) was a Spanish Renaissance architect and sculptor whose career centred on Toledo, where he reshaped cathedral fabric, palace façades, and hospital architecture under imperial Habsburg patronage. Trained in late Gothic workshops yet open to Italianate ornament, he helped define the Plateresque transition into a more classical Spanish Renaissance.

As master of the Toledo cathedral works and designer for the Alcázar and related commissions, he translated courtly and episcopal power into stone at the spiritual capital of Castile. His portals and courtyards balanced heraldic display with structural clarity.

Covarrubias stands among the architects who made Toledo a showcase of sixteenth-century Spanish building.
